offence_severity: Death caused, minimum 7 years to maximum 10 years
physical_harm: Deceased collapsed and died as a result of stabbing
premeditation_planning: Court found no premeditation or planning
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the circumstantial evidence but found that the basic ingredients to support the theory of conspiracy were totally lacking, and there was no specific evidence to link A-10 to any act of conspiracy.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that the murder was witnessed by PWs-22, 23, 24 and 25, and that the prosecution's case relied on their accounts.
post_offence_conduct: A-10 and A-11 fled after the killing of the deceased on 16.07.1994 and were arrested on 27.07.1994. The court considered their conduct in moving from one place to another as part of the circumstantial evidence.
trial_duration: FIR registered on 16.07.1994; charge sheet filed on 15.10.1994; trial judgment dated 25.05.2007; Supreme Court decision dated 17.11.2014
legal_representation: Sushil Kumar, Sr.Adv., Sanjay Jain.Adv. for the Appellant; Madhurima Tatia, Syed Tanweer Ahmad and Mohd. Khairati (for B. Krishna Prasad) Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered on 16.07.1994; charge sheet filed on 15.10.1994; case handed over to CBI on 08.08.1994; investigation commenced on 09.08.1994
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted A-10; High Court: Dismissed appeal of A-10, allowed appeal of A-11; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction and sentence set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that A-10 executed the plan at the instance of A-14, the head conspirator, and that the Appellant was part of a conspiracy to eliminate the deceased. The prosecution also highlighted the Appellant's alleged motive due to his failure to benefit from the deceased's petroleum business and his alleged suit against the deceased.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no conclusive evidence linking A-10 to the conspiracy, and that the acquittals of A-14 and A-11 should have bearing on the conviction of A-10. The defence also contended that the circumstantial evidence was insufficient to establish the Appellant's guilt and that the High Court's findings were legally sound.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principles of circumstantial evidence, requiring that the circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of guilt, and exclude every possible hypothesis of innocence.
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; Arvind Kumar Anuplal Poddar v. State of Maharashtra (2012) 11 SCC 172; Shanti Devi w/o Shanker Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2012) 12 SCC 158
